newsitem.title: UK: UK's Carlton buys classic film collection.
newsitem.headline: UK's Carlton buys classic film collection.

text.p: Carlton Communications Plc has acquired the rights to more than 600 classic films including movies by Buster Keaton, Harold Lloyd and W.C. Fields, the British television company said on Tuesday.

In a deal with the Rohauer Film Collection, Carlton's CTE programme distribution company has bought the UK film rights in perpetuity and the worldwide distribution rights for the next eight years, excluding the Americas. Financial terms were not disclosed.
"The number of television channels worldwide is expanding rapidly and there are new opportunities to screen classic and vintage films," Carlton chairman Michael Green said in a statement.

"In the UK, Carlton will shortly be launching a film channel for digital terrestrial television," Green added. Carlton has joined forces with fellow commercial TV broadcaster Granada Group Plc to launch digital terrestrial subscription services.

CTE's library now contains over 8,000 hours of television programmes, including over 1,500 films. Carlton earlier this year paid 65 million stg for Rank Film Distributors, which has a library of over 700 films.
The Rohauer Collection includes renowned European films such as "The Blue Angel" starring Marlene Dietrich, as well as films by Cocteau and Bunuel.
It also includes "Express Bongo" with Cliff Richard and "Foxhole in Cairo", Michael Caine's first film.
